html:
SMTO-ART-0019 — A file can't be saved while it's still being written

GUID: e793dd55-43bc-4df6-9a1d-96469a3ff550
Slug: artifact-active-writers
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO saves a Task's files only after every command that might write them has finished. A command is still running, or the file has a temporary-looking name, so it wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Task, check whether any command or background job is still running, and wait for it to finish or stop it. SMTO won't save files while something may still be writing them, so you never get a half-written copy.
  2. Open Artifacts from this run and look for the file. SMTO usually adds finished files on its own once commands end, so it may already be saved.
  3. If the file name ends in .tmp, .part, .partial or .lock, or starts with a dot or ~, ask SMTO to save the finished file under a normal name. SMTO treats names like these as unfinished or internal files and never collects them.
  4. If the file is still missing, select Retry collection if it appears, or ask SMTO in a new message to save it. Once nothing is writing the file, SMTO can copy and check it.

What success looks like

  • No commands are still running in the Task, and the file appears once in Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again: look in Artifacts from this run first. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to force a save while the command is still running; you could get an incomplete copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact registration was refused because a writer recorded for the run is not yet in the done state, or temp staging found a path component that discovery rules exclude as unfinished or internal.

What this means

  • Registration finds a writer state other than done, or temporary staging rejects a source-name component marked ineligible by discovery rules. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Registration finds a writer state other than done, or temporary staging rejects a source-name component marked ineligible by discovery rules.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish a live/unresolved writer from an ineligible temporary/partial filename; the latter alone does not prove a live process.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's artifact_collection writers map for entries not in state 'done' (running or unknown jobs, detached terminals, unknown effects) and wait for them to settle or be cancelled. For the temp-staging variant, the source name matches artifact_discovery.eligible exclusions (leading '.' or '~', .tmp, .part, .partial, .lock, .db and similar); have the task write a final file name that is not excluded.
  • Inspect writer state and source eligibility, then collect a stable completed output through the supported flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning writer settles and an eligible stable completed source can be collected.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
